extracted.intended_audience: Authors and reporters of scoping reviews (researchers, journal editors, guideline developers, policy-makers, and other knowledge synthesis stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting scoping reviews using the PRISMA-ScR checklist to ensure complete and transparent reporting of methods and results. Targets how to present title, abstract, methods (search, selection, charting), results, discussion, and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the report as a scoping review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly label the report so readers can immediately recognize the study as a scoping review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (Structured summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a structured summary including, as applicable: background, objectives, eligibility criteria, sources of evidence, charting methods, results and conclusions that relate to the review question(s) and objective(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include core elements (background, objectives, eligibility, sources, charting methods, main results, conclusions). Use a structured abstract format suitable for the target journal or venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of what is already known. Explain why the review question(s)/objective(s) lend themselves to a scoping review approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify why a scoping review (rather than another synthesis type) is appropriate given the state of knowledge and the review objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of the question(s) and objective(s) being addressed with reference to their key elements (e.g., population or participants, concepts and context), or other relevant key elements used to conceptualize the review question(s) and/or objective(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame objectives/questions with key elements (population, concept, context) or an appropriate conceptualization so readers can assess scope and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if a review protocol exists, if and where it can be accessed (e.g., web address), and, if available, provide registration information including registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report existence and location of a protocol and any registration (e.g., OSF), improving transparency and allowing replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the characteristics of the sources of evidence (e.g., years considered, language, publication status) used as criteria for eligibility, and provide a rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State inclusion/exclusion boundaries (dates, languages, publication types) and reasoning behind choices to allow readers to judge comprehensiveness and potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all information sources (e.g., databases with dates of coverage, contact with authors to identify additional sources) in the search, as well as the date the most recent search was executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List databases, grey literature sources, websites, social media, handsearching, contacts with authors, and provide coverage dates and last search date for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the full electronic search strategy for at least one database, including any limits used, such that it could be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete search string(s) for at least one database (and ideally all), including filters/limits, to enable replication; consider including as supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of sources of evidence (process)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the process for selecting sources of evidence (i.e., screening, eligibility) included in the scoping review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe screening and eligibility assessment procedures (e.g., number of reviewers, independent screening, consensus process), and present a flow diagram with numbers screened, excluded (with reasons), and included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data charting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methods of charting data from the included sources of evidence (e.g., piloted forms; forms that have been tested by the team before their use, whether data charting was done independently, in duplicate) and any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the data extraction/charting instruments, piloting, who charted data (single, duplicate), and any procedures to obtain/confirm missing or unclear data from authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all variables for which data were sought and any assumptions and simplifications made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear list of extracted variables (e.g., study characteristics, population, interventions, outcomes, concepts) and note any assumptions or derived variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of individual sources of evidence (if done)
rubrics_metrics.description: If done, provide a rationale for conducting a critical appraisal of included sources of evidence; describe the methods used and how this information was used in any data synthesis (if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear that critical appraisal is optional for scoping reviews; if performed, state the rationale, tools used, and how appraisal informed synthesis or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA items on summary measures (relevant to effect estimates in systematic reviews) are generally not applicable to scoping reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of results (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methods of handling and summarizing the data that were charted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain analytic approaches (e.g., quantitative counts, qualitative thematic/semantic analysis, mapping, evidence mapping visualizations) used to collate, summarize, and report charted data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias across studies (across sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessing risk of bias across studies (e.g., publication bias) is typically not applicable for scoping reviews and is treated as not applicable in PRISMA-ScR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional analyses (if done)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional analyses typical of systematic reviews (e.g., meta-analyses, subgroup/sensitivity analyses) are usually not applicable for scoping reviews; report if any were done and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Selection of sources of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Give numbers of sources of evidence screened, assessed for eligibility, and included in the review, with reasons for exclusions at each stage, ideally using a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts at each stage (identified, screened, eligible, included) and reasons for exclusion; include a flow diagram (e.g., PRISMA-style) to display selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Characteristics of sources of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: For each source of evidence, present characteristics for which data were charted and provide the citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present study/source characteristics (e.g., year, country, population, methods, document type) and cite each included source; consider tables or appendices for detailed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Critical appraisal within sources of evidence (if done)
rubrics_metrics.description: If done, present data on critical appraisal of included sources of evidence (see item 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If critical appraisal was performed, present results (e.g., quality ratings, domains) and explain how these influenced synthesis or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of individual sources of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: For each included source of evidence, present the relevant data that were charted that relate to the review question(s) and objective(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the key extracted data per source relevant to the review questions—this may be presented in tables, narrative summaries, or appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Synthesis of results (presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize and/or present the charting results as they relate to the review question(s) and objective(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an organized presentation/summary of charted findings (e.g., themes, concept maps, frequency counts, evidence types) that addresses the review objectives and relevance to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Risk of bias across studies (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any across-study bias assessment was attempted, report it; otherwise note as not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: Additional analyses (if done)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional analyses were performed (rare for scoping reviews), report methods and findings; otherwise indicate not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: Summary of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the main results (including an overview of concepts, themes, and types of evidence available), explain how they relate to the review question(s) and objectives, and consider the relevance to key groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an interpretive summary tying results back to objectives, outlining major concepts/themes, types and distribution of evidence, and implications for researchers, policy-makers, clinicians, or other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the limitations of the scoping review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge methodological or scope limitations (e.g., language restrictions, search constraints, lack of critical appraisal) and how they might affect findings or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a general interpretation of the results with respect to the review question(s) and objective(s), as well as potential implications and/or next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer overall conclusions, implications for practice/research/policy, and suggestions for future work (e.g., gaps that justify systematic reviews or primary research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe sources of funding for the included sources of evidence, as well as sources of funding for the scoping review. Describe the role of the funders of the scoping review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources for both the included evidence (where known) and the scoping review itself, and disclose any funder influence on design, conduct, analysis, or reporting.
